answer: Each identity claims a velvet tray with a pearl and a crystal, posts an 80 bond, and files the refraction angle through the pearl, serial and temperature included. An auditor recomputes it from the crystal index table; over 2 percent error, reuse, or missing filing burns the bond. The first filing costs 33, the kth 33+6(k-1), the 1000th 6027; 1000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 80,000 locked, each tray needing its own set. A rented-prism ring fails: one shared crystal gives one serial and angle, so the second filing burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 33 once and reclaims the bond after audit.
